item.title: Columbia Square area remains on Office of Violence Prevention’s radar; CPD responds to more than 400 calls this year
item.description:
Claudell Lane in northwest Columbia has been a hotspot for crime through the first week of November, particularly centered around the 1000 block of Columbia Square Apartments.

Columbia police are investigating a shots-fired incident that left three homes and two vehicles damaged Sunday morning, and was connected to a search warrant served in the area Sunday night. On the same street Tuesday night, another shots-fired call led officers to arrest a man who allegedly fired three shots into the air during an argument. No injuries or property damage were reported in that incident.

Including the latest incidents, the CPD dispatch log shows police have responded to 419 calls on Claudell Lane so far in 2026. That included three calls for shots fired or heard, six for an assault and 104 for a disturbance.

item.title: NT Daily 11/9: Downtown Sip & Shop, Nonprofits Feeling the Squeeze & Lincoln Soccer Makes History | Jefferson City News-Tribune
item.description:
It's Monday, November 9, and we're kicking off the week with a look at what's happening around Jefferson City.
Hundreds turned out for Downtown Jefferson City's Sip & Shop over the weekend, local nonprofits are feeling the pressure of rising costs, and a Capital City High School graduate makes history by returning as a teacher.
Plus, Hy-Vee prepares to honor veterans with its annual Veterans Day breakfast, Helias volleyball wraps up an incredible season, and Lincoln University men's soccer makes history with another conference championship and a trip to the NCAA Tournament.
Read more on these stories at newstribune.com.
This episode is brought to you by MU Health Care, Hen House and Coleman Appliance.

item.title: 'My hope is that it can change somebody's life': Columbia family concert raises about $2,500 for free pantry
item.description: Columbia family raises money for their son's Eagle Scout project through a family concert.

item.title: One person arrested after barricade situation on Claudell Lane, police say
item.description: The Columbia Police Department is investigating a shots fired incident in the 1000 block of Claudell Lane that caused property damage.

item.title: Nvidia launches investigation into CEO Jensen Huang over foreign intelligence concerns
item.description: Nvidia announced it is independently investigating its CEO and founder Jensen Huang over concerns he was the target of a foreign intelligence effort.

item.title: MU hopes to expand maternal and child health programs with $6.4 million grant
item.description: A $6.4 million dollar grant will allow two MU programs to continue offering maternal and child health programs and expand them to rural areas.

item.title: Mizzou volleyball sweeps Texas A&M to close home regular season
item.description: Mizzou's win over Texas A&M is the second time in program history that Mizzou has beaten a defending national champion.
